Lets the assistant look things up on Google — news, weather, scores, prices — when you ask something it can\'t answer itself. What you ask is sent to Google Search. Takes effect on the next conversation.
Requires a paid Gemini plan (billing enabled on your API key). On a free key Google refuses it, and the assistant carries on without searching.

On. It also answers the steering-wheel mic button, so both assistants can start at once. Turn it off to leave the button to this app.
Off. The steering-wheel mic button is left to this app. You can turn it back on here.

This switches off the car\'s own voice assistant, so it no longer answers the steering-wheel mic button. Its own voice commands stop working too, until you turn it back on here. Nothing is uninstalled.

If another app (a button mapper, for instance) already uses this button, remove its mapping there — both would otherwise react.

Couldn\'t turn it on automatically — that needs ADB debugging switched on for this head unit. Or, once from a computer: adb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, then try again.
How long the assistant waits in silence before it decides you have finished. A shorter wait answers sooner but may cut you off when you pause in the middle of a sentence.
Keeps the last few exchanges for ten minutes, so a follow-up such as \"do the same for the passenger\" works in the next conversation.
Lets the assistant remember things you ask it to, such as your home address or how you like to be addressed. Kept on this device only.

Start speaking while it is talking and it stops and listens. Turn off if it ever cuts itself off by mistake.
Lets the assistant actually operate car controls, not just talk about them.
This lets the assistant operate the car\'s climate, windows, seats and similar controls when you ask. Use it while parked or when it is safe to do so.

Not confirmed. Open the head unit\'s auto-start screen and switch this app\'s toggle off, so the head unit can start the app by itself. Otherwise it can close the app when the car sleeps or restarts, which turns the steering-wheel button off until you open the app again.

Looks for a new version about every six hours while the internet is available, and shows a notification when there is one. Nothing is installed without your confirmation.

These functions are experimental. They use car functions this app was not designed for, have only been tried on one car model, and may stop working after a car software update. Use them at your own risk.
Lets the assistant speak and play sounds through the car\'s exterior speaker, so people outside hear it. Off by default.
Lets the assistant change the car\'s drive mode (snow, sand, mud, mountain, rock, auto, eco, sport) when you ask. The car still decides whether it accepts. Off by default.

Lets the assistant put an app on the instrument cluster behind the steering wheel and take it off again. The app is shown in the middle of the cluster, where BYD Maps shows its map, and the speed and the warning lights stay visible. Anything shown there is in the driver\'s view, so use it only while the car is parked. It turns BYD Maps on while it works. Off by default.

This is an experimental feature. While an app is on the instrument cluster it is shown in the middle of it, where BYD Maps shows its map, and the speed and the warning lights stay visible. Anything shown there is in the driver\'s view, so only use it while the car is parked. To put an app there it turns BYD\'s navigation app on and off and changes how the cluster is fed, which this app was not made for. It has only been tried on one car model; it may not work, may leave the map showing on the cluster, or may stop working after a car software update. To get the gauges back, ask the assistant to take the app off the cluster, or turn this off. You use it entirely at your own risk and remain responsible for the safe operation of your car.
On: BYD Maps is disabled again once the app has left the cluster and the gauges are back. Off: it stays enabled (it then also appears in the home screen switcher). Off by default.
Speaks the assistant\'s replies on the car\'s own voice channel, the one BYD\'s assistant uses, with a volume of its own, apart from the music.
What happens to the music from the moment the assistant starts listening until the conversation ends.
The music carries on as it is.
The car turns the music down for the conversation with its own dip, which is deep and cannot be changed, and back up afterwards. The music can stop for a moment as it comes back.
The music volume is turned down by the share you choose while the assistant listens and speaks, and put back when the conversation ends. Only while music is playing.
How much to turn the music down
The share of the music volume taken off while the assistant is active.
The music stops for the conversation and starts again afterwards, in apps that start again by themselves.
Listens to the cabin just before it speaks and sets the voice volume to match: louder when the cabin is loud, quieter when it is not.
Louder or quieter than the cabin asks
Moves the volume it picks up or down, about 2 dB a step. In a calm cabin, where the voice is already at its lowest, it makes the voice itself quieter.

This is an experimental feature. It sends the assistant\'s voice and sounds out of the car, which can startle or disturb people nearby, and it works through a car function this app was not made for. It has only been tried on one car model and may stop working after a car software update. You use it entirely at your own risk and remain responsible for how and where it is used.

This is an experimental feature. Changing the drive mode changes how the car delivers power, handles and brakes, and it works through a car function this app was not made for. It has only been tried on one car model; it may not work, or may stop working after a car software update. Only use it when it is safe to do so. You use it entirely at your own risk and remain responsible for the safe operation of your car.
How loud the assistant is when it speaks or plays a sound outside the car. You can also ask for a level by voice, for example \"say it loudly\".

BYD Assistant NG is an independent project. It is not made, approved or supported by BYD or Google; the names BYD, DiLink and Gemini belong to their owners.

The app is provided “as is”, without any warranty. You use it entirely at your own responsibility — including everything it says and everything it does to your car. Vehicle control is experimental: use it only when it is safe to do so, never let it distract you from driving, and check that the car did what you asked.

What you say is sent to Google's Gemini service, and to Google Search if you turn on web search.

BYD Assistant NG is free, open-source software, licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3. You can read the code, report problems and contribute improvements through the project page. Verified vehicle controls for other models are especially welcome.
Kotlin and kotlinx.serialization, AndroidX and Jetpack Compose, OkHttp, Dagger Hilt and Dadb — all open source under the Apache License 2.0. The licence texts are available from each project.
